text:
maria: Quick follow-up to the RFC I posted yesterday about the slice-harvest extraction. I sketched a safety-first cutover plan and wanted quick eyes before I file the PR. TL;DR: incremental extract of the enrichment lane into a new service with a transparent proxy and canary + rewind test harness.

alex: Sounds good, can you call out data ownership boundaries? we need to avoid dual-write ambiguity during the rollover.

maria: Yes — ownership stays with writer until final cut. plan is: 1) read-through proxy -> 2) shadow writes to new service (non-authoritative) -> 3) canary reads from new service for a subset of tenants -> 4) flip on authoritative after pass.

sam: For the shadow phase: how do we validate behavioural parity? small diffing harness or sampling?

maria: We'll use deterministic sample sets + a lightweight diff checker. also adding a "golden prompt" set that triggers edge behavior. If diffs exceed thresholds we halt.

jordan: operational concern: latency. proxy adds extra hop. Can we keep hotpath direct for critical tenants?

maria: Plan includes tenant affinity config. Critical tenants stay direct until validations complete. routing table example:

```
# routing proto (concept)
tenant_route:
  - tenant: critical-co
n    path: direct
  - tenant: beta-corp
    path: proxy->slice-harvest
```

alex: Nice. What about rollback? Need fast failover if the new service misbehaves under load.

maria: We'll run canaries at 1% -> 5% -> 25% traffic. each step has automated SLO checks (p95 latency, error-rate, diff-rate). if any check fails -> immediate traffic drain and route back to direct.

infra-bot: deploy-check: canary pipeline exists for branch `slice-harvest/spike-202` — no blockers found. :white_check_mark:

sam: Testing note: stateful caches and KV consistency are tricky. The new service will expose a read-through cache. we need test harness to simulate cold & warm KV states.

maria: Agree. I'll add a KV warmup job to the canary runbook. Also adding a migrate-metadata flag to mark items as owned by the new service once validated.

jordan: Security/compliance: make sure audit logs show which service authored final writes during the transition. customers will ask.

maria: Yup, audit trail and KMS usage called out in the RFC appendix.

alex: One more: roll-forward vs roll-back decision criteria should be codified (exact thresholds). If someone wants to draft a short spreadsheet with thresholds I can help tune.

maria: I'll draft thresholds and post by EOD. Quick asks: @alex can you review ownership wording? @sam can you outline KV warmup test plan? @jordan can you sanity-check the latency escape hatch?

alex: Will review in the afternoon.

sam: I'll draft KV job and share commands. minimal harness prototype: 
```
./kv-warmup --tenants sample-list.txt --parallel 32 --verify-diff
```

jordan: Look ok from my side. if latency escape makes sense we can cut critical tenants in stages.

maria: Thanks all. If nobody objects I'll open the PR with the safety playbook and the staged rollout script tomorrow morning. :rocket:

alex: +1

sam: +1

jordan: +1

maria: Posted the doc here: https://redwood.example.com/rfcs/slice-harvest-extract -- feedback welcome.
